body.q: A business's cash book shows a bank balance of $4,200 debit. The bank statement shows a balance of $4,650. Which of the following could explain the difference?
body.why: An unpresented cheque reduces the cash book but not yet the bank statement, so the statement balance is higher than the cash book balance.

Unpresented cheques
Outstanding lodgements (deposits not yet credited)
A cheque paid in that the bank has not yet processed
body.q: Which of the following items would require an entry in the cash book when preparing a bank reconciliation?
body.why: Bank charges appear on the statement but not in the cash book, so the cash book must be updated; the other items are timing differences that only affect the reconciliation statement.

body.q: On 31 May, a business's cash book shows a bank balance of $2,800 debit. The bank statement shows a credit of $3,000 for a customer's direct transfer that is not yet in the cash book. What is the updated cash book balance?
body.why: Adding the unrecorded $3,000 receipt to the $2,800 debit balance gives $5,800.

body.q: A cheque received from a customer was paid into the bank but was later returned by the bank marked 'refer to drawer'. How should the business record this in its cash book?
body.why: A dishonoured cheque means the money never arrived, so the earlier debit in the bank column is reversed by a credit.

body.q: Which of the following is the main purpose of preparing a bank reconciliation statement?
body.why: A bank reconciliation compares the cash book with the bank statement to explain differences and detect errors.

body.q: A business has an overdraft. The cash book shows a bank balance of $(1,500) overdrawn. Unpresented cheques total $400 and outstanding lodgements total $900. What balance should the bank statement show?
body.why: Starting from the cash book balance of -1,500, add back unpresented cheques (+400) to get -1,100 and then deduct outstanding lodgements (-900) to get -2,000.

body.q: Which of the following would cause the bank statement balance to be lower than the cash book balance (both in credit)?
body.why: Outstanding lodgements are recorded in the cash book but not yet credited by the bank, so the statement shows a lower balance.

body.q: A business receives its bank statement showing a direct debit of $120 for insurance that has not been entered in the cash book. What entry should be made in the cash book?
body.why: A payment out of the bank account is recorded as a credit in the bank column of the cash book.

body.q: The cash book shows a bank balance of $3,500 debit. Bank interest of $50 charged and a standing order of $200 paid are on the statement but not in the cash book. What is the corrected cash book balance?
body.why: Both items are payments, so deduct them: 3,500 - 50 - 200 = 3,250.

body.q: Which of the following describes an unpresented cheque?
body.why: An unpresented cheque is one the business has written and recorded but which the payee has not yet cashed, so it has not appeared on the bank statement.
